summary: Lisboa is a dense, interlocking Vital Lacerda euro about rebuilding earthquake-ravaged Lisbon, where multi-use cards let you take one of several actions and every building you place has ripple effects across your personal board and the shared city map. It rewards careful long-term planning and engine-building far more than reactive play, and it has a reputation as one of the heaviest, most demanding games in the genre.
praised: strong sense of building a coherent long-term plan
criticised: brutal learning curve and rules overhead
can feel punishing if you fall behind early
not accessible to casual or new gamers

interaction.kind: shared map competition with mostly parallel engines
interaction.detail: Players compete for limited building plots and church/reconstruction tiles on a shared city map, and taking a market action can shift prices for everyone, but most of the depth comes from optimizing your own personal player board and card engine rather than direct conflict.

scoring.why: Points come from building placement, factory production chains, ships, nobility tracks, and end-game bonuses, so the winner is whoever built the most efficient overall engine.
scoring.how_you_win: You win by chaining production and construction actions into an efficient long-term engine that scores across many categories by game end.
